3. The case of the preemptor in thort is that the preemptee-opposite party purchased plot No. 486 and 510 by a registered kabala dated 24.9.1970 at a consideration of Tk. 1,500.00. The preemptor is holding land in plot no. 487 and 488 to the contiguous north of the case land. The preemptor petitioner further stated that the opposite party no. 2 sold the land to the opposite party no. 1 collusively and no notice of transfer has been served upon the preemptor petitioner and after obtaining the certified copy on 31.12.1970 the petitioner came to know about the sale finally and filed the preemption case depositing consideration money along with 10% compensation. The petitioner further stated that there is no impediment in getting the preemption as he has no land more than 10 acres. 

 4. The opposite party no. I preemptee contested the preemption case by filing written objection stating inter alia that the petitioner has got no cause of action for filing the preemption case and he has also no locus standi for filing preemption case. The case is barred by limitation and that the preemption case is bad for defect of parties and stated further that the application is not maintainable as per section 88 and 90 of the E.B. S.A. & T Act. The opposite party further stated the purchased the land within the knowledge of the pre-emptor petitioner and after purchase the petitioner filled up case land at a cost of Tk. 600/- by purchasing earth from Nuruzzaman and in improving the low lying land, the preemptee spent Tk. 2,000.00 and finding such position of land, the preemptor for illegal gain has filed this preemption case on some false plea and that pre-emptee hailed from Barisal and upon purchasing the land and making development of the same has constructed dwelling houses and the pre-emptee-petitioner has been residing therein with his family members and he has no other land other than this property, on the other hand, the preemptor owns substantial land and as such, he sought dismissal of the preemption case. 

 9. The pre-emptee being dissatisfied further with the judgment and decree passed by the Appellate Court filed this revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule as stated above. 

 ‘‘5. Mr. Md. Jani Alam, leaned Advocate appearing on behalf of the pre-emptor opposite party no. 1 submits that the State Acquisition Khatian having recorded the disputed land in the name of the pre-emptor it should be presumed that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in respect of the said disputed land. After what we have stated above with regard to the documentary as well as oral evidence we are unable to attach any importance to the said record of right. It is true that record of right indicates certain right of certain parties but that right is certainly dependent on some material evidence, oral and documentary so as to establish title in favour or persons who claim under the said record of right. The presumption of correctness as to C.S. record of right is not certainly available with regard to the State Acquisition Khatians. There is no. presumption of correctness in respect of the State Acquisition Khatians as it is to be found in case of C.S. Khatians in pursuance of the provision under section 103-B of the Bangal Tenancy Act." 

 12. Mr. Neaz then has placed the provision of section 96 (2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act:- 

 and submitted that holders of land contiguous to the land transferred has not been made party in the preemption case but the courts below allowing pre-emption case have committed error of law. Mr. Neaz further is trying to impress taking to the statement of the preemption application itself to the effect: 

 ‘‘নালিশী ৪৮৬/৫১০ দাগের জমির লাগ উত্তরে দরখাস্ত কারীর সত্য দখলীয় ৮১নং সমসপুর মৌজার ঝ.অ. ২০৪ নং খতিয়ানের ১। আনা জমার অন্তর্গত ৪৮৭ দাগের ২৯ শতাংশ জমি এবং ঐ মৌজার ঝ.অ. ২০২ নং খতিয়ান ॥. আনা জমার অন্তর্গত ৪৪৮ দাগের .২৫ শতাংশ জমি থাকায় দরখাস্তকারী লাগ পাশাইলা হিসাবে" on such statement filed this pre-emption case but not a scrap of paper showing his title filed before the courts but only filed S.A. Khatian in as much as he submitted that the S.A. Khatian is not a deed of title but only such Khatian proves the possession and that S.A. Khatian has no presumption in evidence but the courts below having not recorded any findings as to the title of the pre-emptor have allowed the pre-emption on the basis of S.A. Khatian and allowing pre-emption have committed error of law. 

 Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to the acquisition of such homestead under any law." 

 13. Mr. Shoheb Ahmed Chowdhury, the learned Advocate along with Mr. Syed Anwar Hossain, Advocate has placed the judgments of the courts below, preemption application under section. 96 of SA &T Act and section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and submitted that admittedly, the preemption case was disallowed at first: The pre emptor thereafter, preferred Appeal before the District Judge, Faridpur. The Appellate Court after hearing the parties remanded the case to the Trial Court for holding trial afresh. Thereafter, the preemptor petitioner amended the preemption application adding o party no. 9 Dherandra Nath Roy alias Kalu Roy. The learned Munsif after remand, upon hearing the parties afresh had considered all aspects of the case and upon examination of the evidence and records held that the preemptor is a co-sharer tenant holding land contiguous to the land transferred and further held that the case had not suffered from defect of parties. The learned Munsif also considered the development made by the pre-emptee and granted compensation and thereby, considering all the material aspect of the case had allowed the preemption thereby, committed no error of law and the Appellate Court also considered the judgment of the Trial Court as well as evidence both documentary and oral to its proper perspective and recorded proper findings that the pre-emptor is a tenant holding lands contiguous to the land transferred and the case is not barred by defect of parties and affirmed the judgment of the Trial Court and in the process, the Appellate Court passed the judgment having regard to the order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereby, committed no error of law and as such, calls for no interference by this Hon'ble Court in revision. He further submitted that the facts having been resolved by the courts below concurrently, it does not warrant interference by this Hon'ble court. 

 "9. Admittedly, both the S.A. Khatians as well as RS Khatians in respect of the suit land stand in the names of the predecessor-in interest of the plaintiff-opposite parties and also in some of their names It is true that the SA records, in view of section 19(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act do not provide conclusive evidence as regards title but it provides conclusive evidence as regards their preparation and revision. But entries in the SA records; in my opinion, provide a prima facie evidence as regards title. In order to maintain a suit for declaration under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, the plaintiff is required to have prima facie evidence showing that he has a legal character or right to a property in respect of the subject matter of the suit and granting or refusal to grant a decree in such suit shall always depend on final adjudication thereof on evidence. Since the SA records vide Exts. 3 and 3(ka) stand in the names of the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff opposite parties and also in some of their names it should be taken to be a prima facie evidence of title of the plaintiff-opposite parties in respect of the suit land and, as such, the plaintiff-opposite parties were competent to file the present suit. I do not dispute the legal principles deduced in the aforesaid cases cited by the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners. Since the present suit was not for a declaration of title but for a declaration of the act of the revenue authority namely, the order of mutation outside the purview of law as illegal the same is certainly maintainable. Reference may be made in this connection to the case reported in 16 DLR 298." 

 19. In the facts and circumstances of the case the provision of the Ordinance No. 10 of 1984 does not have any application in the proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the contention of Mr. Bashar fails.
